project_summary: Autonomous single-binary Linux edge DAG scheduler with SQLite WAL state, cgroup v2 per-step isolation, and power-loss catch-up policies.

problem.label: Problem & User Pain
problem.summary: Industrial and retail Linux edge gateways (512MB-1GB RAM) need a zero-dependency local DAG scheduler that survives multi-hour WAN blackouts, power-loss reboots, and runaway child scripts without losing quorum (`dkron-io/dkron#1001`).
edge_cases: WAN blackout lasting 72 hours -> Local cron jobs and sensor pipelines continue executing on schedule via local SQLite WAL.
Hard power loss mid-step -> On reboot, interrupted `RUNNING` attempts are reconciled using the DAG's explicit `catchup_policy`.

scope.label: Scope & Non-Goals
scope.summary: V1 is strictly a single-node Linux binary (`edgecrond` + `edgecron` CLI) executing declarative YAML DAGs with per-node concurrency caps (`dkron-io/dkron#966`); distributed Raft consensus, Windows/macOS executors, and multi-node shared filesystems (`dagucloud/dagu#1260`) are explicit non-goals.
edge_cases: User attempts to configure multi-node Raft clustering -> Rejected at config validation; nodes operate autonomously and sync status asynchronously.
Node overload from 80+ simultaneous scheduled jobs (`dkron-io/dkron#966`) -> Enforces `max_parallel_jobs` per node with bounded FIFO queueing.

memory.label: State, Memory & Agent Communication
memory.summary: Single-writer SQLite3 database in WAL mode (`PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL`, `journal_mode=WAL`) paired with SQLite FTS5 for log search and a bounded 50MB ring buffer per DAG.
edge_cases: 50 parallel steps emitting status heartbeats simultaneously -> Serialized through a single Go writer goroutine committing batched transactions every 100ms (zero `SQLITE_BUSY`).
8GB eMMC flash storage saturation -> Enforces a 50MB rotating ring buffer per DAG and prunes completed run metadata older than 30 days.

bottlenecks.label: Bottlenecks & Failure Modes
bottlenecks.summary: Eliminates double-forked orphan leaks and memory overruns by placing each step in an ephemeral Linux cgroup v2 scope (`/sys/fs/cgroup/edgecron/<run-id>/<step-id>`) with `memory.max` and `cgroup.kill`, and prevents reboot cron stampedes via `catchup_policy`.
edge_cases: Step spawns background subshells and times out or crashes -> Writing `1` to `cgroup.kill` atomically terminates all descendant PIDs.
4-hour power outage with a 1-minute cron (`dagucloud/dagu#695`) -> `catchup_policy: latest_only` runs exactly 1 catch-up instance instead of 240 simultaneous processes.

differentiation.label: Prior-Art Differentiation
differentiation.summary: Directly addresses verified pain points in `dkron-io/dkron` (`#1001` Raft quorum loss on pod restart/IP change, `#966` missing per-node parallel job limit, `#712` failure-only webhooks) and `dagucloud/dagu` (`#1260` shared-filesystem coupling for workers, `#695` date-bounded cron replay), while avoiding the abandonment seen in dormant Go schedulers `shunfei/cronsun` and `wj596/gojob`.
edge_cases: Avoids `dkron-io/dkron#1001` (cluster unrecoverable without wiping Raft data after dual-node restart) by eliminating Raft in favor of autonomous per-node SQLite WAL.
Solves `dagucloud/dagu#1260` and `dkron-io/dkron#966` by bundling an mTLS `sync_outbox` push agent and strict per-node `max_parallel_jobs` + Linux cgroup v2 step isolation.

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Cryptographic dependency locking and reproducible static Go builds
tooling_recommendations.why: Verifies exact module SHA-256 checksums with `CGO_ENABLED=0` for zero-libc-drift Linux ARM64/AMD64 binaries.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: Vendored `vendor/` tree in git (bloats diffs); dynamically linked CGo dependencies (breaks across older factory glibc versions).

tooling_recommendations.purpose: CGo-free embedded SQLite WAL engine and cron schedule parser
tooling_recommendations.why: Scouted via `scout.py -t`: `modernc-org/sqlite` (BSD-3-Clause) compiles SQLite to pure Go without CGo, and `flc1125/go-cron` (MIT) provides cron parsing with second/descriptor support.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: mattn/go-sqlite3 (requires CGo and cross-compiler toolchains); etcd/boltdb (lacks relational SQL + FTS5 log indexing).

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Multi-stage static binary build and privileged cgroups v2 integration test container
tooling_recommendations.why: Proven across scouted incumbents (`dkron-io/dkron`, `dagucloud/dagu`); lets CI test cgroup v2 `memory.max` and `cgroup.kill` behavior reproducibly.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: Host-only `go test` (cannot safely simulate OOM kills or power-loss recovery on developer laptops).

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Automated cross-arch matrix builds, race-detector tests (`go test -race`), and static analysis
tooling_recommendations.why: Proven in `dkron-io/dkron` and `dagucloud/dagu`; catches concurrency bugs in the single-writer SQLite channel on every PR.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: Manual local release builds (high risk of shipping untested ARM64 binaries).

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Multi-cluster central hub orchestration for >1,000 edge gateways
tooling_recommendations.why: Defer until the central observability hub is built in V2; V1 targets single-binary systemd deployment on individual edge nodes (`docker-compose.yml` for local dev).
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: systemd unit + single static binary (selected NOW for Day-1 edge node deployment).

memory_architecture.agent_communication_pattern: Single-writer Go channel (`chan StateTransition`) batching step heartbeats from worker goroutines into SQLite WAL every 100ms; asynchronous mTLS push outbox (`sync_outbox`) to hub.
memory_architecture.workflow_memory_flow: Append-only `dag_runs` and `step_attempts` state transitions committed with `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL`, paired with SQLite FTS5 over structured step stderr/stdout logs (`step_logs_fts`) and a 50MB ring-buffer cap.
memory_architecture.rationale: EdgeCron schedules deterministic DAG transitions and searches exact exit codes/error symbols in local step logs. Embedded SQLite WAL + FTS5 provides ACID crash recovery and fast exact log search with zero external daemons, avoiding the Raft quorum loss seen in `dkron-io/dkron#1001` and the shared-filesystem coupling in `dagucloud/dagu#1260`.
memory_architecture.alternatives_considered: Embedded etcd/Raft (`dkron-io/dkron#1001` — loses cluster quorum when 2 of 3 nodes restart or change IP); Flat YAML/JSON status files (`dagucloud/dagu#1260` — requires shared filesystem across workers); Vector DB / RAG (unnecessary overhead for deterministic state and exact log tokens).
failure_modes: SQLITE_BUSY lock contention under 50+ concurrent step heartbeats -> Mitigated by funneling all writes through a single Go channel batching commits every 100ms.
Unbounded disk growth on 8GB industrial eMMC flash -> Mitigated by 50MB per-DAG ring buffer and automatic 30-day run history pruning.

red_team_critiques.title: Post-Outage Reboot Stampede on High-Frequency Schedules
red_team_critiques.attack: If an edge node loses power for 4 hours and has a 1-minute cron job, firing all 240 missed runs simultaneously on boot will exhaust 1GB RAM and corrupt local sensor state.
red_team_critiques.mitigation: Require an explicit `catchup_policy` (`skip`, `latest_only`, or `backfill_serial` with date bounds as requested in `dagucloud/dagu#695`), defaulting to `latest_only`.

red_team_critiques.title: Unprivileged Or cgroup v1 Kernel Fallback
red_team_critiques.attack: Edge gateways running older Linux kernels without unified cgroups v2 hierarchy or running `edgecrond` as a non-root user without delegated cgroup permissions will fail to create `/sys/fs/cgroup/edgecron/*`.
red_team_critiques.mitigation: Run a startup pre-check verifying `/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers` delegation; fail fast with a clear `systemd` `Delegate=yes` unit snippet or explicitly require `--allow-pgid-fallback` (`Setpgid: true` + `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`).

flowchart TB
    subgraph EdgeNode["Linux Edge Gateway (512MB–1GB RAM)"]

system_design.sequence_mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Timer as Cron / Catchup Planner
    participant Sem as Node Concurrency Semaphore
    participant Cgroup as Linux cgroup v2 Runner
    participant Writer as Single-Writer SQLite Loop
    participant DB as SQLite WAL (state.db)

    Timer->>Sem: Evaluate missed window (catchup_policy=latest_only)
    Sem->>Writer: Enqueue Transition(RUN_STARTED)
    Writer->>DB: Batch Commit (100ms window)
    Sem->>Cgroup: Spawn step in /sys/fs/cgroup/edgecron/run-1/step-1
    alt Step Succeeds Within Timeout & Memory Cap
        Cgroup-->>Sem: Exit 0 + Ring-Buffer Logs
        Sem->>Writer: Enqueue Transition(STEP_SUCCEEDED)
    else Step Times Out or Exceeds memory.max
        Cgroup->>Cgroup: Write 1 to cgroup.kill (reaps all child PIDs)
        Cgroup-->>Sem: Exit SIGKILL / OOM
        Sem->>Writer: Enqueue Transition(STEP_FAILED) + Failure Webhook
    end
    Writer->>DB: Batch Commit + Enqueue sync_outbox

options_matrix.cons: Loses quorum on 2-node restart or IP change (`dkron-io/dkron#1001`); 200MB+ RAM
Requires shared NFS/filesystem across workers (`dagucloud/dagu#1260`); no cgroup v2 kill

options_matrix.option: Autonomous SQLite WAL + Linux cgroups v2 (`EdgeCron`)
options_matrix.pros: 100% offline availability, zero orphan processes, <15MB RAM
options_matrix.cons: Single-node execution scope (no cross-node DAG steps)

implementation_steps: Bootstrap Go 1.23 module, pure-Go SQLite WAL schema (`dag_runs`, `step_attempts`, `step_logs_fts`, `sync_outbox`), and single-writer 100ms batch channel (`ADR-0001`)
Implement Linux cgroups v2 step runner (`memory.max`, `cpu.max`, `cgroup.kill`) with `Setpgid` fallback and per-node `max_parallel_jobs` semaphore (`ADR-0002`, `dkron-io/dkron#966`)
Implement DAG YAML parser, cron schedule planner (`flc1125/go-cron`), and power-loss `catchup_policy` (`skip`, `latest_only`, `backfill_serial`, `dagucloud/dagu#695`)
Implement failure-only webhook notifier (`dkron-io/dkron#712`), 50MB FTS5 log ring-buffer pruning, and asynchronous mTLS `sync_outbox` hub pusher (`dagucloud/dagu#1260`)
